The test image shows a tomato **stem lesion at a branch junction**. Key features:
- Tan/cream-colored bleached lesion on the stem/branch
- White cottony-looking growth on the lesion surface
- The branch coming off the junction appears wilted/dead (brown dried foliage on right)
- Tissue appears desiccated and girdled

Top candidates: **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white cotton mycelium, bleached stem), **Gray_Mold** (tan-brown stem lesions at junctions), **Southern_Blight** (white mycelium at stem base).

The bleached, girdled stem with what appears to be white cottony mycelium strongly points to Sclerotinia. Let me check one reference image.

The Sclerotinia reference shows bleached, hardened stem tissue with white mycelium and black sclerotia at soil line. The test image shares the bleached/cream stem tissue but shows the lesion at a **branch junction** with the branch dead/wilted above it, and appears to have some white cottony material.

**Analysis:**
- Bleached, cream/tan hardened stem tissue matches Sclerotinia's "bleached and hardened" description
- White cottony surface material consistent with Sclerotinia mycelium
- The wilted/dead branch above the girdled lesion matches both Gray Mold and Sclerotinia
- Gray Mold would show gray-brown fuzzy spore mass more prominently
- The very pale/bleached color (almost cream-white) leans more toward Sclerotinia than Botrytis (which is tan-brown)
